answer: Echo-density admission. Each node must sustain a minimum count of distinct, reciprocal neighbors whose round-trip latency variance stays within a kernel of tolerance across successive sampling windows; the topology itself becomes the credential. A fresh identity at dawn has no established echoes, so its traffic is relayed only as whisper-weight until reciprocal links accumulate. Attackers must run many real, geographically spread nodes with stable links over time, making each accepted identity cost sustained infrastructure and latency coordination rather than a fake signature.
